A steady pulse with subtle changes or a restless beat that keeps surprising you?

Describe a moment when a crowd started clapping along and changed the energy of a performance.
Have you ever listened to an instrumental track mainly to hear how its rhythm develops?
What can a singer communicate through their voice before you understand any lyrics?

prompts.text: What's an everyday sound you've heard and thought might belong in a piece of music?
A producer gives you only the sounds of a kitchen to create a short beat. What could become the rhythm?
Tell me about hearing an unusual sound effect in a song and wondering how it was created.
Creative production often starts with listening to ordinary noises in a new way.
Recording rain against a window or the rhythm of footsteps on different surfaces?
A small background sound can give a recording a distinctive sense of place.
Do you prefer music with layers you can discover or arrangements where every element feels immediately clear?
You can sample one sound from a railway station, a market or a forest. What would you listen for?
Describe a recording in which silence or room noise became an important part of the atmosphere.
What would you want to ask a producer about a track with a sound you can't identify?
What makes you want to listen to an album from beginning to end rather than choose individual tracks?
Tell me about an album whose final song changed how you understood its opening.
You have twelve good songs but space for eight on an album. What would you use to choose the order?
An album can tell a story through its sound even when the lyrics don't form a single narrative.
A record with a consistent atmosphere or one that moves through several surprising musical styles?
The transition between two songs sometimes becomes a favourite moment in its own right.
Have you ever changed your opinion about a track because of where it appeared in an album?
A friend asks you to choose the closing track for a compilation of shared memories. What kind of feeling would you leave them with?
Describe an album you returned to years later and appreciated for a different reason.
What's the difference between a collection of favourite songs and an album you think works as one piece?
What's a song that seems to get an entire room involved, regardless of who picked it?
Tell me about singing along with strangers when you didn't expect to know the words.
A community wants a musical event open to people who don't perform. How would you make participation feel easy?
A shared song can create a moment of connection without everyone knowing each other.
A large crowd singing one melody together or a small circle learning a song by listening?
Sometimes people become more confident singers when they realise nobody is evaluating them.
Have you noticed certain songs taking on new significance at weddings, graduations or community gatherings?
You're preparing a song for an event with several generations present. What would you ask about the audience first?
Describe a time music helped people feel comfortable in a place that was new to them.
What makes a singalong welcoming to someone who's never heard the song before?
Which song did an older person introduce you to that changed how you hear older music?
Tell me about discovering the favourite artist of somebody in your family.
You can play three modern songs for someone who grew up sixty years ago. How would you choose what to share?
An old recording often reveals as much about its listeners today as about the people who first heard it.
Comparing two generations' dance songs or hearing how each chose music for celebrations?
A song considered daring in one era can later become familiar background music.
Have you ever realised a new song borrowed a musical idea from a recording much older than you expected?
Your grandfather or grandmother offers to play a song from their youth. What would you ask before pressing play?
Describe a moment when you and someone from another generation unexpectedly agreed about an artist.
What does the music people pass down through families reveal about everyday life at different times?
Can you think of an instrumental piece that tells you a story without using a voice?
Tell me about a film or game scene where the music helped you understand something the characters never said.
You must choose a short instrumental piece to accompany a film of a peaceful afternoon. What sounds would you look for?
An instrumental melody can leave room for listeners to imagine very different stories.
A sparse piano theme with long pauses or an orchestral piece that slowly adds instruments?
Music without lyrics can sometimes make its audience pay more attention to small changes in texture.
What kinds of images appear in your mind when you listen to music without a singer?
A composer wants to suggest the feeling of arriving home without using any recognisable sound effect. How might they begin?
Describe being surprised by how strongly a quiet instrumental section affected you.
How does your attention change when a piece of music has no words for you to follow?
Have you ever been drawn to a piece of music because its cover artwork made you curious?
Tell me about discovering that an album's visual identity had a meaning you hadn't noticed.
A musician gives you one song and asks for a cover design. What would you listen for before sketching?
The best music artwork can create a feeling without illustrating the lyrics literally.
A bold abstract cover with no photograph or a quiet portrait that suggests a story?
A distinctive cover can help listeners recognise an album decades after its release.
Do you think artwork changes the way you imagine music before your first listen?
You need to design two covers for the same song, one playful and one reflective. Which details would change?
Describe a music video, poster or album sleeve whose design stayed with you longer than you expected.
What would make you recognise a musician's visual style even if their name wasn't on the artwork?
What's a traditional musical style you've heard but don't yet know much about?
Tell me about attending a cultural celebration where a musical performance taught you something unexpected.
An elder invites you to hear a song passed down in their community. What would be respectful questions to ask?
A musical tradition is easier to appreciate when you understand how people actually use it.
Learning the history of a ceremonial drum rhythm or seeing how a traditional dance connects to live music?
Musical traditions can keep evolving without losing the stories that make them meaningful.
How does music's purpose change when it is part of everyday work rather than a staged performance?
You are helping document a local music tradition for younger listeners. What information belongs beside the recordings?
Describe a performance where you were interested in the relationship between the musicians and the audience.
What could modern musicians learn from musical traditions that rely on oral teaching?
What's a piece of music that took several listens before something clicked for you?
Tell me about revisiting a familiar song after a long break and noticing a detail you'd missed.
You have to help a friend appreciate an unfamiliar musical style without insisting they like it. What do you play first?
Music can become more interesting when we listen for a question rather than just whether we enjoy it.
Concentrating on the bass line through a whole song or noticing how the backing vocals change each chorus?
A listener's mood can make a familiar recording seem to have a different pace or colour.
Have you ever tried listening to a song while paying attention to only one instrument?
An audio engineer plays you three versions of the same recording with tiny differences. What would you try to identify?
Describe an experience that helped you understand music you had previously found confusing.
What would you like to hear differently the next time you listen to your favourite album?
